issue.title: Published sase-core-rs floor lacks the nested memory.glossary scope diagnostic
issue.description:
Proposed by epic sase-ia's land agent (sase-ia.land) while landing 'Move glossary and amd_h1_title under a new memory config section'. Caused by sase-ia, but externally blocked: the fix cannot land until sase-core cuts a release.

WHAT IS WRONG: epic phase sase-ia.1 taught the Rust config provenance pass to emit the glossary_scope error for a non-local 'memory.glossary', not just the legacy top-level 'glossary'. That change is sase-core commit 480299b ('fix(config): diagnose nested glossary scope'), which landed on sase-core master AFTER the v0.21.3 release tag. Verified: 'git merge-base --is-ancestor c8c1f2c 480299b' succeeds (c8c1f2c is 'chore: release v0.21.3') and 'git tag --contains 480299b' is empty. sase's pyproject.toml declares 'sase-core-rs>=0.21.3,<0.22.0'.

IMPACT: on any environment that resolves sase-core-rs from PyPI, a 'memory.glossary' block placed in a user, overlay, plugin, or builtin config layer produces no glossary_scope diagnostic from 'sase config layers' or 'sase doctor'. The legacy top-level 'glossary' key is still diagnosed at 0.21.3, so the epic's own migration guidance ('use memory.glossary') is precisely the path that loses the scope guard. Nothing crashes and no reader misbehaves -- the Python glossary loaders only read project-local config either way -- so the only loss is the warning.

WHY NO EXISTING GATE CATCHES IT: CI's published-core-minimum-smoke lane runs tools/check_sase_core_rs_bindings, which checks that required *bindings* exist. glossary_scope is behavior inside an already-present binding, so the lane stays green. Dev installs and CI's build-core job both build sase_core_rs from sase-core HEAD, which has the fix, so 'just check-full' also stays green. Nothing will fail when the floor is stale -- the gap is silent and could persist across many releases.

BLOCKED ON: a sase-core release containing 480299b. Nothing in this repo can proceed before that; bumping the floor now would make 'uv lock' unresolvable.

SCOPE once that release is on PyPI: raise pyproject.toml's sase-core-rs floor to that version, refresh uv.lock, update the declared-minimum assertion in tests/test_sase_core_rs_telemetry_smoke_tool.py::test_declared_minimum_tracks_pyproject_dependency, and re-run 'just check-full'. Consider whether the published-core smoke lane should assert this behavior (not just binding presence) so the next instance of this skew class is caught mechanically.

PRIOR ART (same skew class, version-specific and already satisfied by 1cd532915 and d7e9ae8ae): sase-hz (0.21.0 -> 0.21.1 glossary bindings, still READY though the floor is now 0.21.3) and sase-h0 (0.19.2 -> 0.19.3 snooze-note contract). Not a duplicate of either: those name a different missing behavior and a different target release.
